Figure 8:A learning rate that supports useful new-task learning can still cause uneven losses across prior capabilities.The complete main sweep contains 36 SFT runs: three model rows, two update-task
columns, three learning rates, and two seeds. Each run uses 256 selected input
rows for one epoch. Cells show seed-mean percentage-point score change from
the pre-update model. The top row of each panel is new-task gain. Horizontal
rules separate it from three displayed bank tasks and four held-out tasks.
Color uses one common scale saturated at±10\pm 10pp. Printed values preserve larger magnitudes. At1e-5, several
conditions lose new-task accuracy as well as prior-task accuracy, indicating
failed adaptation rather than a necessary retention–acquisition trade-off.
Bank tasks are replay-eligible evaluation tasks. No replay is used in these SFT runs.
These are endpoint comparisons across learning rates, not training trajectories.
The full capability profiles appear in AppendixD.
